We've changed some intent here.  Old intent was to walk through
Name1
Name2
Name3

In order, and stop on the last available.

This code (which claims to just be a refactor) would now allow skipping indexes, so we could potentially accept Name1, Name3.... with Name2 missing.  That wasn't the intent originally.  Maybe that was on purpose but just not documented in the commit message?

It also now allows "NameFoo" as a valid input, whereas the previous code would not, which messes up the hwmonNames being an indexable list of entries.

I asked @rickyaz@meta.com to also add a "Fixes" reference.  Ultimately this was all broke with `838bd71374cf ("hwmontempsensor: Add support for BME280")`.  The Name properties are no longer a "indexable list of entries" anyhow.  I don't know how we would know what to skip and what not to skip; ultimately I think that is a sensor-specific piece of information.

The BME280 sensor being added in the breaking commit has a different set of hardware than the HDC1080, which is what we're observing being broken.  HDC1080 had { "temperature", "humidity" } only and the original code had "humidity" as "index 2".  The BME280 change moved humidity to "index 3", whatever that means, probably because the BME280 has { "temperature", "pressure", "humidity" } but this seems to have broken the existing humidity sensors (which only had 2 'metrics).

Are there actually cases now where the index is still important?

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/82560 introduced changes to entity-manager and HwmonTempMain.cpp (changing name# -> name<string>).  The processing of the read config would ignore invalid "NameFoo", but I could specifically add checks for valid values (Name, NamePressure, NameHumidity).

LMK if you think it's worth it.
Done
